newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: YTL sees Zimbabwe deal proceeding.
newsitem.headline: YTL sees Zimbabwe deal proceeding.

text.p: Malaysia's YTL Corp Bhd said on Tuesday it expects a power privatisation deal with the Zimbabwean government to go ahead despite objections raised by some power industry officials in that country.

"In spite of incriminations (from certain Zimbabwean parties) the (Zimbabwean) government has granted us everything we have asked for," YTL group managing director Francis Yeoh told reporters. "We are absolutely very confident of what we are going to put up there."
YTL, a power and infrastructure firm, signed a letter of intent with the Zimbabwean government on September 16 for the privatisation of the Hwange Power station in northern Zimbabwe.

Zimbabwe Electricity Supply Authority (ZESA) officials have criticised the deal, saying it did not conform to the country's policy of empowering the indigenous black majority population of the country.

But senior Zimbabwean government officials have defended YTL's involvement in the $580 million deal which, when completed, would increase Hwange power station's generation capacity to 1,590 megawatts, from 920 megawatts.
"This is something we have to face when investing in a developing country," Yeoh said, when asked about the difficulties in the deal.
Asked if the glitch in the negotiations would result in a delay of the project, Yeoh said: "These are commercial contingencies we have to face."
At the close of morning trading on Tuesday, YTL stock was up 10 cents at 14.30 ringgit.
